applied.runtime: adapter builds LocalExecutionPolicy from effective sets and F1b/F1c fields; later per-operation denial is policy_denial / local_policy_rejected
applied.control_plane: no CP outcome; F4/F5 adapter would apply narrowed values
applied.can_authorize_action_reason: effective = caller INTERSECT record, a subset of both; it can only remove permissions the caller already held. operationally_authorized is always False. Passing a policy check is necessary, never sufficient: the grant, approval, claim and commit check still decide.

runtime.detail: registry_code null; decision_kind applied_deny_all; deny_all_fields list; selection and record identity

applied_deny_all.backstop: LocalExecutionPolicy accepts empty frozensets; if the adapter constructs it anyway, check() denies as local_policy_rejected with free text only, so the adapter must record registry_deny_all first (adapter contract).

control_plane.open: OPEN-Q6: may the F4/F5 adapter emit deny; doc 06 finding 9 says deny is emitted by one adapter only

applied_deny_all.can_authorize_action_reason: An empty dimension permits nothing; the result is a restriction, so it cannot authorize any action.

overlay_not_applied.can_authorize_action_reason: The caller policy is the host own policy, unchanged; the registry contributed nothing and an action is authorized only by the OCS grant path.

required_policy_unavailable.can_authorize_action_reason: effective is None and the caller policy is never returned (decision.py).
